title: The Slow Path to Agreement
text:
Treaties are rarely the product of a single meeting. They emerge from months of quiet consultation, in which officials test each other's positions and identify areas of possible compromise. Public announcements often hide this slow process, making agreements appear sudden when they were in fact carefully prepared.

Diplomatic failures are also instructive. A negotiation that collapses may reveal that one party misjudged the other's priorities or overestimated its own leverage. Historians often learn more from these breakdowns than from successful accords, because they expose assumptions that were previously unexamined.

questions.text: Why might agreements seem sudden to the public?
options: Because they were in fact sudden
Because the preparation behind them is usually hidden

questions.text: What can be inferred about why diplomatic breakdowns are instructive?
options: They show that negotiation is always pointless
They expose assumptions that were not examined before
They prove that compromise never happens
